title: Dell PowerEdge R770AP Review One Fast Intel Xeon 6 Server
gist: Review of the Dell PowerEdge R770AP, a 2U air-cooled dual-socket server supporting two 128-core Xeon 6980P CPUs (256 cores) with up to 32 front E3.S bays. Kennedy notes Intel could not supply Clearwater Forest chips and sees this as the main Intel platform given the Diamond Rapids schedule; the excerpt covers hardware only, not benchmarks.

insights.claim: The R770AP supports up to two Intel Xeon 6980P processors with 128 cores each for 256 cores total in a 2U air-cooled dual-socket chassis.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Core density is the key spec for consolidation economics.
insights.locator: The Dell PowerEdge R770AP is a 2U air-cooled

insights.claim: Given the current Diamond Rapids schedule, the Xeon 6 AP platform is set to be the major Intel platform for some time, and Intel could not supply Xeon 6+ Clearwater Forest chips for this review.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Signals Intel roadmap delays or supply constraints for next-gen server parts.
insights.quote: Intel could not get us chips
insights.locator: Given the current Diamond Rapids schedule

insights.claim: Moving to E3.S gives up to 32 front drive bays, 16 per side with a central air channel, versus fewer than 24 U.2 bays on earlier 2.5-inch designs that reserved the center for airflow.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: EDSFF adoption lifts NVMe density per chassis.
insights.locator: Having the center area dedicated for airflow

insights.claim: Dell lists front storage options of up to 32x E3.S Gen5 NVMe, up to 16x 2.5-inch U.2 Gen5 NVMe, or no backplane.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Configurability lets buyers trade density against form-factor compatibility.
insights.locator: Dell's current product specifications list front storage options

insights.claim: The BOSS-N1 rear boot module with two 480GB M.2 NVMe drives provides RAID 1 for OSes such as VMware or Windows Server and frees two front bays.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Small design details raise usable front-bay count.
insights.locator: The Dell BOSS-N1 DC-MHS boot solution

insights.claim: The server uses redundant 1.8kW power supplies and OCP NIC 3.0 cards for networking, with Broadcom BCM57608 and ConnectX-6 Dx installed, and 200Gbps QSFP56 ports.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Modular NICs support high-speed fabrics in general-purpose servers.
insights.locator: The power supplies here are redundant 1.8kW units

insights.claim: Shared $200 VGA monitors on data center carts keep analog VGA in use even on five-figure dual-socket servers.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Legacy interfaces persist because of installed operational practice.
insights.locator: The VGA connector provides the analog console path

insights.claim: Fitting higher-power NICs, DPUs and GPUs in the rear requires significant thermal design effort because SSDs, CPUs and memory heat the air before it reaches the rear risers.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Thermal design limits accelerator density in air-cooled servers.
insights.locator: On the rear, Dell has many riser configurations

insights.claim: Xeon 6 can easily run 400Gbps NICs (1x 400G or 2x 200G), and faster networking helps feed the high-end AP processors.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Fast NIC support is a requirement for high-core-count platforms.
insights.locator: In this generation, many will use lower-speed 10G and 25G

insights.claim: NICs have not risen in cost as much as memory and storage, so upgrading networking in new clusters is becoming a more popular way to raise overall cluster performance.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Memory and storage inflation shifts spend toward networking upgrades, benefiting NIC vendors.
insights.quote: NICs have not risen in cost as much as memory and storage
insights.locator: In this generation, many will use lower-speed 10G and 25G
